    Dune Meadows: Contrasts at an Explicit Environmental Covariate

    dune-covariate-adjusted-contrasts.Rmd

    Management differences can vary along the continuous A1 environmental gradient. A contrast from a model containing Management * A1 therefore has no unique meaning until a reference value of A1 is declared. Phase 20 makes that value part of the estimand and records it in every result.

    dune_environment <- data.frame(
  Management = droplevels(dune.env$Management),
  Use = droplevels(dune.env$Use),
  A1 = dune.env$A1
)
dune_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management * A1 + Use,
  dune_environment,
  vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
)
a1_reference <- mean(dune_environment$A1)

    derive_adjusted_means() fixes A1 at the supplied value and averages the categorical nuisance factor Use over a declared reference distribution. Equal weighting gives every use level the same influence; proportional weighting reproduces their observed frequencies.

    adjusted_means <- derive_adjusted_means(
  dune_design,
  factor = "Management",
  at = c(A1 = a1_reference),
  weights = "equal"
)
adjusted_means$reference_values
#>   A1 
#> 4.85
adjusted_means$coefficient_rows
#>    (Intercept) ManagementHF ManagementNM ManagementSF   A1         Use.L Use.Q
#> BF           1            0            0            0 4.85 -1.387779e-16     0
#> HF           1            1            0            0 4.85 -1.387779e-16     0
#> NM           1            0            1            0 4.85 -1.387779e-16     0
#> SF           1            0            0            1 4.85 -1.387779e-16     0
#>    ManagementHF:A1 ManagementNM:A1 ManagementSF:A1
#> BF            0.00            0.00            0.00
#> HF            4.85            0.00            0.00
#> NM            0.00            4.85            0.00
#> SF            0.00            0.00            4.85

    The planned comparisons below are one-degree-of-freedom general linear hypotheses on those adjusted coefficient rows. Each receives a contrast-specific Freedman–Lane residual permutation while retaining all other fitted directions as nuisance structure.

    planned <- rbind(
  `BF - HF` = c(BF = 1, HF = -1, NM = 0, SF = 0),
  `managed pair - other pair` =
    c(BF = 0.5, HF = 0.5, NM = -0.5, SF = -0.5)
)

planned_fit <- permanova_adjusted_contrasts(
  dune_design,
  factor = "Management",
  contrasts = planned,
  at = c(A1 = a1_reference),
  weights = "equal",
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260721
)
planned_fit
#> Explicitly covariate-adjusted distance contrasts
#> Reference values: A1=4.85 
#> Family: user-specified explicitly covariate-adjusted contrasts 
#>                   contrast weighting df         ss denominator_df  pseudo_f
#>                    BF - HF     equal  1 0.09987203             10 0.6277811
#>  managed pair - other pair     equal  1 0.09535882             10 0.5994117
#>  p_perm p_adjusted adjustment
#>    0.65          1       holm
#>    0.68          1       holm
    pairwise_fit <- permanova_adjusted_pairwise(
  dune_design,
  factor = "Management",
  at = c(A1 = a1_reference),
  weights = "proportional",
  adjust = "holm",
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260721
)
pairwise_fit
#> Explicitly covariate-adjusted distance contrasts
#> Reference values: A1=4.85 
#> Family: all pairwise explicitly covariate-adjusted contrasts 
#>  contrast    weighting df         ss denominator_df  pseudo_f p_perm p_adjusted

#>   BF - NM proportional  1 0.10397912             10 0.6535977  0.630      1.000
#>   BF - SF proportional  1 0.09031949             10 0.5677352  0.695      1.000
#>   HF - NM proportional  1 0.47050369             10 2.9575180  0.040      0.240
#>   HF - SF proportional  1 0.26285354             10 1.6522592  0.155      0.620
#>   NM - SF proportional  1 0.34143267             10 2.1461963  0.095      0.475

    Changing at changes the question whenever the target factor interacts with the covariate. The functions never infer this value from the observations. They also reject random effects, aliased fixed models, unsupported predictor classes, and incomplete reference specifications rather than silently substituting an average.
